subject: ILCE-6400 updater enforcement gate map

gates.summary: The outer α6400 updater was mapped far enough to identify its signed Sony engine and the engine's FirmwareData DAT integrity parser, but no authenticated writable firmware image was recovered.

evidence.claim: The updater wrapper contains a signed Sony System Software Updater engine whose SHA-256 is pinned by this report.
The engine searches for FirmwareData*.dat, verifies a trailing DEND marker and CRC, and parses DATV, PROV, FDAT, and UDID container tags.
ModelName.ini supplies display text appended to the updater window; these references do not perform the enforcement comparison.
The host engine appears to integrity-check and stage an opaque DAT rather than decrypting feature binaries in this function.
The complete wrapper-to-FirmwareData extraction path and any additional host authenticity checks are not yet characterized.

gates.next_experiment: Trace every caller and data reference around the DAT buffer, CRC result, and updater resource extraction without executing the updater against a device.
gates.feature_relevance: This layer must yield authenticated target and donor contents before Vertical UI, full touch UI, or Creative Looks code and resources can be compared.

gates.summary: The updater's Windows storage and SCSI boundary is statically mapped, while the disconnected run proved that no physical device was opened and no protocol exchange was observed.

evidence.claim: The sandboxed disconnected-camera run recorded zero device-open groups and did not reach a camera protocol boundary.
The signed engine opens a selected storage volume and issues DeviceIoControl requests 0x002d1400 and 0x002d0c00.
A 0x44-byte pass-through structure with a 0x2c-byte header and 0x12-byte sense region is submitted through DeviceIoControl request 0x0004d014.
Request 0x0004d014 and the observed structure are consistent with Windows SCSI_PASS_THROUGH_DIRECT transport.
Exact command descriptor block bytes, response lengths, retry semantics, and a real-camera trace remain unobserved.

gates.next_experiment: Recover the command descriptor construction and response parsing statically, then model only exact recovered exchanges in the synthetic fail-closed harness.
gates.feature_relevance: Transport knowledge can explain how an official package is delivered, but it does not establish that newer UI or color-processing components are compatible with α6400 hardware or firmware.

gates.summary: The host-side command state machine and returned model/version error codes are visible, but the enforcing camera logic and any bypass remain unknown.

evidence.claim: The host state machine uses command IDs 0x01, 0x10, 0x20, 0x30, 0x40, 0x100, and 0x200 for initialization, guard, version, mode switch, write, completion, and state operations.
The host validates response format/status value 1 and requires the returned command field to match the requested command.

Requests use a zero-initialized 32-byte header followed by optional data: data length is at offset 0x00, a firmware-derived 16-bit value at 0x04, command at 0x06, and a wrapping sequence value at 0x0a.
Returned statuses 0x140 and 0x141 select the invalid-model error path, while 0x142 selects the invalid-version error path.
Because these errors are decoded from the guard response, model and version enforcement likely occurs in the camera updater rather than through the display-only ModelName.ini value.
The camera-side comparison inputs, signature decision, anti-rollback behavior, command authorization, and failure recovery state machine have not been recovered.
No change that safely bypasses statuses 0x140, 0x141, or 0x142 has been identified or tested.

gates.next_experiment: Map the 32-byte host command header and guard-response fields exactly, then search authenticated updater contents for the corresponding camera-side dispatcher and status constants.
gates.feature_relevance: Passing this gate would only permit package acceptance; it would not supply α6400-compatible Vertical UI, touch widgets, event routing, or Creative Look image-processing tables.

gates.summary: No authenticated α6400 boot chain, recovery loader, firmware signature root, partition map, or rollback path has been recovered.

evidence.claim: All mutations remain quarantined, camera execution is false, and no experiment produced an installable image.
Host package acceptance cannot demonstrate that a modified image would pass camera boot verification or remain recoverable.
Boot ROM trust anchors, stage signatures, partition redundancy, rollback counters, and an independently verified unbrick route are unknown.

gates.next_experiment: Recover authenticated partition and signature metadata from firmware contents and validate a restore path on a nonessential α6400 body before considering any camera execution.
gates.feature_relevance: Even a correctly ported feature would be unusable if the modified image cannot boot or if a failed boot cannot be recovered.

gates.summary: No authenticated α6400 runtime loader, module ABI, code-signing policy, integrity monitor, memory budget, or UI/image-pipeline extension boundary is available.

evidence.claim: The dependency matrix contains no authenticated α6400 layout selector, portrait renderer, menu-wide touch dispatcher, widget binding, or Creative Look processing table.
The donor FDAT regions remain opaque, so executable modules, resources, relocations, and processor-specific dependencies have not been identified.
Existing α6400 orientation and limited touch capabilities make target-specific implementation conceivable but do not prove a compatible donor ABI or safe patch boundary.
Runtime signature checks, module loading, watchdog behavior, graphics resources, input routing, image-processor interfaces, and memory limits remain unknown.

gates.next_experiment: After authenticated decryption, build symbol and structure maps for target UI, input, graphics, and color-pipeline components before proposing any patch site.
gates.feature_relevance: This is the layer where Vertical UI, full touch UI, and Creative Looks must actually execute; none of their target integration points has been recovered.

feature_assessment.evidence_gap: Orientation state exists on α6400, but the portrait layout selector, renderer transform, rotated hit testing, resources, and ABI are unlocated.
Shooting-screen touch exists, but menu-wide dispatch, widgets, bindings, geometry, and a safe extension point are unlocated.
Practical Creative Style approximations exist, but native base tables, extra adjustment axes, color-pipeline code, and processor compatibility are unlocated.

conclusion: Static reverse engineering moved the boundary from an unknown Windows wrapper to a mapped host parser, storage transport, command state machine, and camera-returned model/version statuses. That is meaningful progress, but it is not a bypass: decryption, camera-side enforcement, boot trust, recovery, runtime integrity, and all native feature integration points remain unresolved.
